guide.title: AI Memory MCP
guide.setup_body: Three steps: get a token, configure the client, verify one call.
step1.title: Get a token
step1.body: An admin issues it. The plaintext shows once, so copy it at once.
contact.caption: Scan with WeChat, or
step2.title: Configure the client
step2.body: Paste the block below into your MCP client (mcp.json).
step2.cursor: In Cursor: Settings → MCP → Add new MCP server, then paste the URL below.
step3.title: Verify one call
step3.body: Ask it to remember one thing, then ask it back in a new chat.
step3.figure_alt: Chat showing a memory stored and a memory id returned
step3.caption: A real chat: the summary is stored and the memory id comes back.
agents.intro: Any MCP-capable client works. These are the ones we verified.
tools.intro: These eight tools are yours. Ask in plain words; the client picks the tool.
tools.store.does: Save a memory. Same title and category merge. Kept 7 days by default, can be permanent.
tools.store.eg: “Remember: my meeting notes are always bullet points.”
tools.recall.does: Find memories by meaning, ranked by relevance, importance and recent use. The way to search in Chinese.
tools.recall.eg: “What was that note format I mentioned last time?”
tools.search.does: Find by exact keywords. Every word must appear.
tools.get.does: Read one memory in full by its id.
tools.list.does: List memories by category, age or source. Up to 200.
tools.list.eg: “List everything I saved about writing style.”
tools.family.does: Load the most recent entries of one category.
tools.smart.does: Say what you want in one line; it picks the category and loads it.
tools.caps.does: Show the current tier and tool count. Always available.
tools.caps.eg: “Which tools can I use right now?”
tools.note: The tier is fixed by the server. Changing your client config will not change it, and you must reconnect after a change.
users.title: Users
users.lead: Invite only, no self-signup. Creating a user also prepares its own database.
users.empty: No users yet. Create the first one.
users.caption: Each user has its own database. Paths are monospaced for character-level checks.
users.invalid: Lowercase letters, digits, underscore and hyphen only.
users.error: The user could not be created. Check the username.
detail.tokens.lead: Plaintext shows once. Tokens of one user share one memory.
detail.error.userDisabled: That user is deactivated. Restore access first, then issue a token.
detail.col.label: Label
detail.diag.lead: Check here before looking at a user session.
dlg.issue.title: Issue a token
dlg.issue.body: The plaintext shows once. Copy it into the client now.
dlg.issue.label: Label
dlg.issue.label_note: One token per device. Revoke one without touching the others.
dlg.revoke.title: Revoke this token?
dlg.revoke.body: New sessions are refused and open sessions end. Other tokens and existing memory are unaffected.
dlg.rotate.title: Rotate this token?
dlg.rotate.body: The old token is revoked and a new one is issued. Memory is unaffected.
dlg.target.label: Label
audit.title: Audit
audit.lead: Five event types. Session rows carry the resolved database path.
audit.empty: No events match. Clear the user or widen the range.
audit.note: No token plaintext, no memory content. A refused session writes nothing, so it has no path.
cap.title: Capacity
cap.lead: Session limits are ours. Memory and storage quotas come from upstream. Over-limit is refused, not queued.
cap.readonly: Read only. Limits are set in the server config; change them there and restart. This page never writes.
cap.q.lead: Seven keys, set explicitly to the upstream defaults. Omitting them delegates silently.
cap.note: Over-limit requests are refused. The storage quota counts the database only, not WAL or temp files.
ag.title: Admin MCP config
ag.lead: For admins: how you sign in, and the two ways your AI client connects.
ag.tier.body: The tier is fixed by the server. Change it, then reconnect.
ag.stdio.body: Run the container on the same host.
ag.ssh.body: Connect over SSH. The forced command pins the tier.
gal.title: Mockups
gal.lead: Six pages, one stylesheet, four languages. Variants open with query parameters.
admins.signin.body: Your identity is the email or Google account listed in the Cloudflare Access policy. There is no password in this portal, so there is nothing to reset.
admins.keys.body: List at least two emails in the policy. Any one of them gets you in, so losing a mailbox is not a lockout.
admins.keys.i1: Two or more emails listed in the policy
admins.keys.i2: A Google account set as the primary login
admins.session.body: A session lasts about a month today. Three months is the target; the platform may cap it lower. A new device asks you to verify again.
admins.fallback.body: Sign in to Cloudflare to change the policy, or use the SSH path, which never goes through this portal.
admins.manage.note: Admins are added and removed in Cloudflare Zero Trust. This page only shows how it works.
detail.danger.lead: Revokes every token at once and refuses new sessions. The memory database stays on disk.
detail.danger.note: Reversible: use Restore access to lift the deactivation, then issue a new token. Deleting the database is a separate, server-side decision.
dlg.deact.title: Deactivate {handle}?
dlg.deact.body: Every token is revoked and new sessions are refused. The memory database is kept; issue a new token to restore access.
cap.how.where_v: On the host: compose env for session limits, config file for upstream quotas.
cap.how.restart_v: Restart the portal so the new limits apply. Quotas apply on the next session.
cap.how.tier_v: The tier is per client. Set it in Admin MCP config, not here.
admins.cf.where_v: Cloudflare Zero Trust → Access → Applications → your admin host.
admins.cf.session_v: 1 month is the console cap; longer needs the API. Applies to new logins.
admins.cf.login_v: Google is primary, email one-time code is the backup. A new device asks again.
admins.cf.who_v: The emails in the Allow policy. Add a second one so a lost mailbox is not a lockout.
admins.add.v: Add the email to the Allow policy and save. They sign in with it — nothing for you to send.
admins.remove.v: Delete the email from that Allow policy. Access ends on their next request; there is no session to revoke.
admins.nopw.v: There is no portal password to set or reset. A new device verifies again.
users.error.handle.traversal: Usernames cannot contain a slash or "..".
users.error.handle.pattern: Use lowercase letters, digits, underscore and hyphen only.
users.error.directory: The user directory could not be created. Check that /data/users is writable.
detail.error.directory: The user directory is not writable. Check /data/users.
detail.issued.title: Copy this token now
detail.issued.body: The plaintext appears once and cannot be retrieved later.
detail.diag.w1: Startup checks pass. The access checks arrive with the next batch.

admin.unauthorized.title: Sign in required
admin.unauthorized.body: This portal has no password. Sign-in is handled by Cloudflare Access.
devLogin.title: Development sign-in
devLogin.lead: This page exists only on loopback development. It signs you in with the self-signed test token produced by --dev-login — the same test channel the E2E suite uses. Production never registers this route.
devLogin.noToken: No test token found. Start the portal with the dev script --dev-login first.
unauth.diag.channelOn: The self-signed test channel is ENABLED on this instance, so you can sign in from this page.
unauth.diag.channelOff: The self-signed test channel is disabled — sign-in must come from Cloudflare Access.
detail.issued.expired: The plaintext is no longer available — it is shown only once. Issue a new token if you still need one.
